topic.title: Kubernetes NetworkPolicies: Controlling Pod-to-Pod and Pod-to-External Traffic
topic.shortdesc: Learn how Kubernetes NetworkPolicies define allowed ingress and egress traffic for pods using label selectors, namespaces, and ports.

body.p: [{'section_title': 'What a NetworkPolicy does', 'content': 'A NetworkPolicy is a namespaced resource that selects a set of pods and specifies which traffic is allowed to and from those pods; enforcement depends on your CNI plugin supporting NetworkPolicy.'}, {'section_title': 'Prerequisites and enforcement model', 'content': 'Verify your cluster uses a NetworkPolicy-capable CNI (for example Calico, Cilium, or Antrea); without enforcement, policies are accepted by the API but do not change traffic behavior.'}, {'section_title': 'Core concepts: podSelector, namespaceSelector, ipBlock', 'content': 'Use podSelector to target pods in the policy’s namespace, namespaceSelector to match peer namespaces, and ipBlock to allow/deny CIDRs for external endpoints (ipBlock cannot select cluster pods directly).'}, {'section_title': 'Ingress rules', 'content': 'Ingress rules allow traffic to selected pods from specific peers (pods/namespaces/IP blocks) and optionally restrict by protocol and port; if any ingress rules exist, only the allowed sources can reach the selected pods.'}, {'section_title': 'Egress rules', 'content': 'Egress rules allow traffic from selected pods to specific peers and ports; if any egress rules exist, only the allowed destinations are reachable from the selected pods.'}, {'section_title': 'Default deny patterns', 'content': 'Create a policy with an empty ingress list to deny all inbound traffic to selected pods, and/or an empty egress list to deny all outbound traffic; apply carefully to avoid breaking DNS, metrics, or control-plane dependencies.'}, {'section_title': 'Common allowances (DNS, intra-namespace, app-to-db)', 'content': 'Typical policies explicitly allow egress to kube-dns/CoreDNS on UDP/TCP 53, allow ingress from an ingress controller namespace, and allow app-to-database traffic by selecting the database pods and port (for example TCP 5432).'}, {'section_title': 'Troubleshooting and validation', 'content': 'Confirm pod labels and namespace labels match selectors, check policy ordering/combination (policies are additive), and validate with connectivity tests (for example exec + curl/nc) while inspecting CNI-specific logs or flow observability tools.'}]
